description: High-roof passenger minibus running intercity routes and tourist transfers from Bangkok van terminals.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: High-roof passenger minibus, long slab sides with a sliding side door and a row of tinted windows, short flat nose with a low grille and large windscreen, roof-mounted air conditioner pod, rear barn doors, steel wheels Materials: White painted panels with a coloured route stripe along the sides, tinted glass, chrome door handles, dust and road film along the lower sills, sun-chalked roof.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Toyota Commuter / Toyota Motor. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 6,412/8,000 triangles, 4/6 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two canvases at 1.7 MB, factory ~150 ms. Colliders hand-padded to the envelope with a front-bumper box and measured: 8 boxes, coverage 0.957.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.88 x 2.27 x 5.38 m over the body (mirrors to 2.14) against the declared 1.88 x 2.28 x 5.38; the proxy is 2.09 lengths tall against the real 2.36, a 13 percent declared-aspect residual on the band table.
featureReviews.notes: Heights off the proxy (roof 1.00 H, belt 0.55 H, wheel top 0.29 H, sill 0.18 H); stations nose 0.03 L, screen base 0.10 L, roof from 0.22 L, tail 0.99 L; four glass bays a side with the sliding door between B and C. Second pass: the proxy side and end depth maps read column by column -- screen base 0.05 L, one r 1.75 m roof dome to 0.30 L, r 0.30 rear corner, 0.80 W at 0.80 H -- and the slab replaced by a filleted, smooth-shaded sweep with a rounded AC pod; the slab read is gone at every azimuth. Third pass: screen base at z 2.58 over the bumper, bulged and wrapped.

featureReviews.evidence: Black window gaskets along the belt and drip rail, a dark lower valance under the bumper, dusty dark steel rims; blunt rounded nose, two-bar grille and slot between lamps yawed round the corner, bumper corners wrapped round nose and tail; windscreen VISIBLE as glass with a cowl and two wiper arms on it (it had been paint under the full-width A-pillar sweep since the first build); rear-door pane, shut line and tail-lamp posts; mirrors, handles, three belt stripes, door rail, sill steps, shut lines.
featureReviews.notes: Built as tinted boxes on one white material, each standing proud of the shell.

featureReviews.evidence: Four instanced wheels off one lathe with the rim a step apart from the tyre; pivots wheel-front-l/r and wheel-rear-l/r on the axle at each hub, exposed on sculptRuntime.
featureReviews.notes: Dusty dark pressed-steel wheels in the plate (region-tyre 0.86, rim #5f5c57): dished rim #5c5248 with a #2e2620 vent ring against tyre #5e5750 with #4a443d lugs; the third build rims were a pale #8a877f.

featureReviews.evidence: White #d7dadf on the material as the envelope; dust as a smooth zoned mud canvas at the linear ratio of #b6b4b0 (lower flank #8a8985 over upper #a7a7a7, 0.82), solid at the sill, out at 0.92 m, 0.16 film, 90 streaks and 1,500 specks behind both wheels, roof keyed clean -- the third build laid a 0.72 ratio on as 260 streaks and 4,500 specks and rendered the flank #62615f against the plate #8a8985. Glass re-based to the plate screen tone #58676d with a sill-to-top tile down to #303a3e; stripes faded to the plate #a3a3a0.
featureReviews.notes: Ratio formed in linear space; roof kept clean by height-keyed UVs. Residual: the harness shades the white flank to luma ~133 where the plate top-lit render holds 167.

notes: 5.38 m long and 2.28 m tall, both above the vehicle category's prior, which is correct for a high-roof commuter van and puts it in the hero budget class. The tall flat sides and the roof AC pod are the silhouette that separates it from a delivery van. No destruction groups.
